topics.title: Error in Book (Introduction to Counting and Prob.)
topics.text:
Question 8.12, pg 131 of AoPS Introduction to Counting and Probability, the question states,



[quote]Grunters and Screamers are playing a Championship. The two teams will play each other until one has won 4 games at which the winner is declared. Grunters have 75% probability and Screamers have 25% probability to win an individual game.



What is the probability that the Grunters will win the Grand Championship in exactly 7 games?

[/quote]



We know that Grunters obviously win the last, ie 7th game. So we just need to find the probability in which Grunters win 3 games and Screamers win 3 games. One such game will be of form (G = Grunters win, S = Screamers win)



GGGSSS



Probability for this to happen is ${ \left( \frac { 3 }{ 4 }  \right)  }^{ 3 }{ \left( \frac { 1 }{ 4 }  \right)  }^{ 3 } = \frac{3^3}{4^6}$



Note: every game in which Grunters win 3 times and Screamers win 3 times will have same probability.



Total number of ways in which Grunters win 3 times and Screamers win 3 times is $\left( \begin{matrix} 6 \\ 3 \end{matrix} \right) = 20$



Hence the answer is $20\left( \frac { 3^{ 3 } }{ 4^{ 6 } }  \right) = \frac{135}{1024}$.



In the book however, the probability is taken for matches of form GGGGSSS. This is incorrect because if we do that, we are also counting possibilities of form SGGGGSS because if Screamers win the last match, then Grunthers have already won 4 matches before.

topics.title: rate time problem
topics.text:
Ed drives to work at a constant speed S. One day he is halfway to work when he immediately turns around,  speeds up by 8 mph, and drives home. As soon as he is home, he turns around and drives to work at 6 mph faster than he drove home. His total driving time is exactly 67% greater than usual.

Find S in mph.





what didn't work for meLet the total time it takes for Ed to drive from home to work be $\ t$. Let the total distance from home to work be $\ d$. His usual speed is $\ s$.

On this particular day, we have three different time intervals: 1) when he goes halfway 2) he goes back home from halfway 3) he goes from home to work:

1) $\ t=\dfrac{d}{2s} $

2) $\ t=\dfrac{d}{2(s+8)} $

3) $\ t =\dfrac{d}{s+14} $

If all of this is exactly 67% greater than usual - $\dfrac{d}{s}$ - then we can write an equation like:



\[\dfrac{d}{2s}+\dfrac{d}{2(s+8)}+\dfrac{d}{s+14} \, = \, \dfrac{167d}{100s} \]

After nasty algebra, we end up with:



\[ 46s^2+1287s+7952 = 0 \]

. . . which gives values of s around -9 and -18.



The correct answer should be a positive whole number . . . .




I'm pretty sure I didn't mess up in my algebra, but maybe I did. However, is this method correct?



Thanks :)



EDIT: Correct AnswerAnswer should be 42 lol




Ok nvm I'm just bad at algebra. The first big equation is correct; i just messed up somewhere in between.

\[\dfrac{d}{2s}+\dfrac{d}{2(s+8)}+\dfrac{d}{s+14} \, = \, \dfrac{167d}{100s} \]gives the correct answer.

Does anyone have fast ways to solve this?

topics.title: Mock MathCOUNTS State Target #7 - Tyson Reflects
topics.text: Tyson creates a sequence of points in the following way: First, he selects a random $a_1$. To move from $a_n$ to $a_{n+1}$, he reflects $a_n$ over the lines $x = n$ and $y = n$ . If the sum of the x-coordinates and y-coordinates of $a_k$ and $a_{k+1}$ is $2016$, find $k$.

topics.title: Mock MathCOUNTS State Target #8 - 2D becomes 3D
topics.text: John saws a thirty-inch wooden board into four pieces using parallel cuts perpendicular to the thirty-inch-long side of the board. The four pieces have a total length of thirty inches. What is the probability none of the boards have length greater than eight inches? Express as a common fraction.

topics.title: A penguin will walk from (0,0) to (9,5) by moving either one
topics.text: A penguin will walk from (0,0) to (9,5) by moving either one unit up or one unit to the right each minute. Define a turn to be a point where the penguin changes from going up to right or from going right to up. How many paths have 5 turns?

topics.title: Mock MathCOUNTS State Sprint #22 - Doubles Tennis
topics.text: Eleven male tennis players and nine female tennis players are in a room together. Let $s$ be the number of single-gender (only male or only female) doubles teams that can be made. Let $m$ be the number of mixed-gender doubles (one male, one female) teams that can be made. Find $|s - m|$.

topics.title: Mock MathCOUNTS State Sprint #23 - Ascending Sequence
topics.text: $2016$ is the $N$th term of the ascending sequence that starts $0, 1, 2, 6, 10, 11, 12, 16 \cdots$ and consists of all distinct whole numbers that can be made using the digits $0, 1, 2$ and $6$. Find $N$.

topics.title: A word from us
topics.text: greetings people of aops. i will be co-moderator on this part of the forum along with tare (and MysticTerminator as of September 9th). if any of you have questions that need to be answered, or any interesting challenges, go ahead. im going to try my best to keep discussions on track, teach interesting concepts, and bring up cool bean challenges. mostly, ill be getting questions from mathcounts (chapter, state, nationals), and amc (8, 10, and maybe 12). i may post some "hard" questions that would suit better on the amc thread, but they may teach good concepts. im not going to limit myself to mathcounts and amc questions though. ill keep it on that level though. any questions or suggestions go ahead. and please dont get offended if i delete any of your posts. ill try my best not to, but if they're really off topic, ill go ahead. other than that, ill try to be as helpful as my limits go. and we all will benefit from this. HAPPY SOLVING!
